Nothing of importance remained."}, {"paragraph": 77, "text": ""There's that," said Tuppence suddenly, pointing to a small, old-fashioned safe let into the wall."}, {"paragraph": 78, "text": "The key was in the lock, and Julius swung open the door, and searched inside."}, {"paragraph": 79, "text": ""Well," said Tuppence impatiently."}, {"paragraph": 80, "text": "There was a pause before Julius answered, then he withdrew his head and shut to the door."}, {"paragraph": 81, "text": ""Nothing," he said."}, {"paragraph": 82, "text": "In five minutes a brisk young doctor arrived."}, {"paragraph": 83, "text": ""Heart failure, or possibly an overdose of some sleeping-draught." He sniffed. "Rather an odour of chloral in the air.""}, {"paragraph": 84, "text": "Tuppence remembered the glass she had upset. A new thought drove her to the washstand. She found the little bottle from which Mrs. Vandemeyer had poured a few drops."}, {"paragraph": 85, "text": "It had been three parts full. Now-- _it was empty_."}], "013.source": [{"paragraph": 1, "text": "FRIDAY and Saturday passed uneventfully. Tuppence had received a brief
answer to her appeal from Mr. Carter. In it he pointed out that the
Young Adventurers had undertaken the work at their own risk, and had
been fully warned of the dangers. If anything had happened to Tommy he
regretted it deeply, but he could do nothing."}, {"paragraph": 2, "text": "This was cold comfort. Somehow, without Tommy, all the savour went out
of the adventure, and, for the first time, Tuppence felt doubtful of
success. While they had been together she had never questioned it for
a minute. Although she was accustomed to take the lead, and to pride
herself on her quick-wittedness, in reality she had relied upon Tommy
more than she realized at the time. There was something so eminently
sober and clear-headed about him, his common sense and soundness of
vision were so unvarying, that without him Tuppence felt much like a
rudderless ship. It was curious that Julius, who was undoubtedly much
cleverer than Tommy, did not give her the same feeling of support. She
had accused Tommy of being a pessimist, and it is certain that he
always saw the disadvantages and difficulties which she herself was
optimistically given to overlooking, but nevertheless she had really
relied a good deal on his judgment. He might be slow, but he was very
sure."}, {"paragraph": 3, "text": "It seemed to the girl that, for the first time, she realized the
sinister character of the mission they had undertaken so lightheartedly.
It had begun like a page of romance. Now, shorn of its glamour, it
seemed to be turning to grim reality. Tommy--that was all that mattered.
Many times in the day Tuppence blinked the tears out of her eyes
resolutely. “Little fool,” she would apostrophize herself, “don’t
snivel. Of course you’re fond of him. You’ve known him all your life.
But there’s no need to be sentimental about it.”"}, {"paragraph": 4, "text": "In the meantime, nothing more was seen of Boris. He did not come to the
flat, and Julius and the car waited in vain. Tuppence gave herself over
to new meditations. Whilst admitting the truth of Julius’s objections,
she had nevertheless not entirely relinquished the idea of appealing to
Sir James Peel Edgerton. Indeed, she had gone so far as to look up his
address in the _Red Book_. Had he meant to warn her that day? If so,
why? Surely she was at least entitled to demand an explanation. He had
looked at her so kindly. Perhaps he might tell them something concerning
Mrs. Vandemeyer which might lead to a clue to Tommy’s whereabouts."}, {"paragraph": 5, "text": "Anyway, Tuppence decided, with her usual shake of the shoulders, it was
worth trying, and try it she would. Sunday was her afternoon out. She
would meet Julius, persuade him to her point of view, and they would
beard the lion in his den."}, {"paragraph": 6, "text": "When the day arrived Julius needed a considerable amount of persuading,
but Tuppence held firm. “It can do no harm,” was what she always came
back to. In the end Julius gave in, and they proceeded in the car to
Carlton House Terrace."}, {"paragraph": 7, "text": "The door was opened by an irreproachable butler. Tuppence felt a little
nervous. After all, perhaps it _was_ colossal cheek on her part. She
had decided not to ask if Sir James was “at home,” but to adopt a more
personal attitude."}, {"paragraph": 8, "text": "“Will you ask Sir James if I can see him for a few minutes? I have an
important message for him.”"}, {"paragraph": 9, "text": "The butler retired, returning a moment or two later."}, {"paragraph": 10, "text": "“Sir James will see you. Will you step this way?”"}, {"paragraph": 11, "text": "He ushered them into a room at the back of the house, furnished as a
library. The collection of books was a magnificent one, and Tuppence
noticed that all one wall was devoted to works on crime and criminology.
There were several deep-padded leather arm-chairs, and an old-fashioned
open hearth. In the window was a big roll-top desk strewn with papers at
which the master of the house was sitting."}, {"paragraph": 12, "text": "He rose as they entered."}, {"paragraph": 13, "text": "“You have a message for me? Ah”--he recognized Tuppence with a
smile--“it’s you, is it? Brought a message from Mrs. Vandemeyer, I
suppose?”"}, {"paragraph": 14, "text": "“Not exactly,” said Tuppence. “In fact, I’m afraid I only said that to
be quite sure of getting in. Oh, by the way, this is Mr. Hersheimmer,
Sir James Peel Edgerton.”"}, {"paragraph": 15, "text": "“Pleased to meet you,” said the American, shooting out a hand."}, {"paragraph": 16, "text": "“Won’t you both sit down?” asked Sir James. He drew forward two chairs."}, {"paragraph": 17, "text": "“Sir James,” said Tuppence, plunging boldly, “I dare say you will think
it is most awful cheek of me coming here like this. Because, of course,
it’s nothing whatever to do with you, and then you’re a very important
person, and of course Tommy and I are very unimportant.” She paused for
breath."}, {"paragraph": 18, "text": "“Tommy?” queried Sir James, looking across at the American."}, {"paragraph": 19, "text": "“No, that’s Julius,” explained Tuppence. “I’m rather nervous, and that
makes me tell it badly. What I really want to know is what you meant by
what you said to me the other day? Did you mean to warn me against Mrs.
Vandemeyer? You did, didn’t you?”"}, {"paragraph": 20, "text": "“My dear young lady, as far as I recollect I only mentioned that there
were equally good situations to be obtained elsewhere.”"}, {"paragraph": 21, "text": "“Yes, I know. But it was a hint, wasn’t it?”"}, {"paragraph": 22, "text": "“Well, perhaps it was,” admitted Sir James gravely."}, {"paragraph": 23, "text": "“Well, I want to know more. I want to know just _why_ you gave me a
hint.”"}, {"paragraph": 24, "text": "Sir James smiled at her earnestness."}, {"paragraph": 25, "text": "“Suppose the lady brings a libel action against me for defamation of
character?”"}, {"paragraph": 26, "text": "“Of course,” said Tuppence. “I know lawyers are always dreadfully
careful. But can’t we say ‘without prejudice’ first, and then say just
what we want to.”"}, {"paragraph": 27, "text": "“Well,” said Sir James, still smiling, “without prejudice, then, if I
had a young sister forced to earn her living, I should not like to see
her in Mrs. Vandemeyer’s service. I felt it incumbent on me just to give
you a hint. It is no place for a young and inexperienced girl. That is
all I can tell you.”"}, {"paragraph": 28, "text": "“I see,” said Tuppence thoughtfully. “Thank you very much. But I’m not
_really_ inexperienced, you know. I knew perfectly that she was a bad
lot when I went there--as a matter of fact that’s _why_ I went----” She
broke off, seeing some bewilderment on the lawyer’s face, and went on:
“I think perhaps I’d better tell you the whole story, Sir James. I’ve a
sort of feeling that you’d know in a minute if I didn’t tell the truth,
and so you might as well know all about it from the beginning. What do
you think, Julius?”"}, {"paragraph": 29, "text": "“As you’re bent on it, I’d go right ahead with the facts,” replied the
American, who had so far sat in silence."}, {"paragraph": 30, "text": "“Yes, tell me all about it,” said Sir James. “I want to know who Tommy
is.”"}, {"paragraph": 31, "text": "Thus encouraged Tuppence plunged into her tale, and the lawyer listened
with close attention."}, {"paragraph": 32, "text": "“Very interesting,” he said, when she finished. “A great deal of what
you tell me, child, is already known to me. I’ve had certain theories
of my own about this Jane Finn. You’ve done extraordinarily well so
far, but it’s rather too bad of--what do you know him as?--Mr. Carter to
pitchfork you two young things into an affair of this kind. By the
way, where did Mr. Hersheimmer come in originally? You didn’t make that
clear?”"}, {"paragraph": 33, "text": "Julius answered for himself."}, {"paragraph": 34, "text": "“I’m Jane’s first cousin,” he explained, returning the lawyer’s keen
gaze."}, {"paragraph": 35, "text": "“Ah!”"}, {"paragraph": 36, "text": "“Oh, Sir James,” broke out Tuppence, “what do you think has become of
Tommy?”"}, {"paragraph": 37, "text": "“H’m.” The lawyer rose, and paced slowly up and down. “When you arrived,
young lady, I was just packing up my traps. Going to Scotland by the
night train for a few days’ fishing. But there are different kinds of
fishing. I’ve a good mind to stay, and see if we can’t get on the track
of that young chap.”"}, {"paragraph": 38, "text": "“Oh!” Tuppence clasped her hands ecstatically."}, {"paragraph": 39, "text": "“All the same, as I said before, it’s too bad of--of Carter to set you
two babies on a job like this. Now, don’t get offended, Miss--er----”"}, {"paragraph": 40, "text": "“Cowley. Prudence Cowley. But my friends call me Tuppence.”"}, {"paragraph": 41, "text": "“Well, Miss Tuppence, then, as I’m certainly going to be a friend. Don’t
be offended because I think you’re young. Youth is a failing only too
easily outgrown. Now, about this young Tommy of yours----”"}, {"paragraph": 42, "text": "“Yes.” Tuppence clasped her hands."}, {"paragraph": 43, "text": "“Frankly, things look bad for him. He’s been butting in somewhere where
he wasn’t wanted. Not a doubt of it. But don’t give up hope.”"}, {"paragraph": 44, "text": "“And you really will help us? There, Julius! He didn’t want me to come,”
 she added by way of explanation."}, {"paragraph": 45, "text": "“H’m,” said the lawyer, favouring Julius with another keen glance. “And
why was that?”"}, {"paragraph": 46, "text": "“I reckoned it would be no good worrying you with a petty little
business like this.”"}, {"paragraph": 47, "text": "“I see.” He paused a moment. “This petty little business, as you call
it, bears directly on a very big business, bigger perhaps than either
you or Miss Tuppence know. If this boy is alive, he may have very
valuable information to give us. Therefore, we must find him.”"}, {"paragraph": 48, "text": "“Yes, but how?” cried Tuppence. “I’ve tried to think of everything.”"}, {"paragraph": 49, "text": "Sir James smiled."}, {"paragraph": 50, "text": "“And yet there’s one person quite near at hand who in all probability
knows where he is, or at all events where he is likely to be.”"}, {"paragraph": 51, "text": "“Who is that?” asked Tuppence, puzzled."}, {"paragraph": 52, "text": "“Mrs. Vandemeyer.”"}, {"paragraph": 53, "text": "“Yes, but she’d never tell us.”"}, {"paragraph": 54, "text": "“Ah, that is where I come in. I think it quite likely that I shall be
able to make Mrs. Vandemeyer tell me what I want to know.”"}, {"paragraph": 55, "text": "“How?” demanded Tuppence, opening her eyes very wide."}, {"paragraph": 56, "text": "“Oh, just by asking her questions,” replied Sir James easily. “That’s
the way we do it, you know.”"}, {"paragraph": 57, "text": "He tapped with his finger on the table, and Tuppence felt again the
intense power that radiated from the man."}, {"paragraph": 58, "text": "“And if she won’t tell?” asked Julius suddenly."}, {"paragraph": 59, "text": "“I think she will. I have one or two powerful levers. Still, in that
unlikely event, there is always the possibility of bribery.”"}, {"paragraph": 60, "text": "“Sure. And that’s where I come in!” cried Julius, bringing his fist down
on the table with a bang. “You can count on me, if necessary, for one
million dollars. Yes, sir, one million dollars!”"}, {"paragraph": 61, "text": "Sir James sat down and subjected Julius to a long scrutiny."}, {"paragraph": 62, "text": "“Mr. Hersheimmer,” he said at last, “that is a very large sum.”"}, {"paragraph": 63, "text": "“I guess it’ll have to be. These aren’t the kind of folk to offer
sixpence to.”"}, {"paragraph": 64, "text": "“At the present rate of exchange it amounts to considerably over two
hundred and fifty thousand pounds.”"}, {"paragraph": 65, "text": "“That’s so. Maybe you think I’m talking through my hat, but I can
deliver the goods all right, with enough over to spare for your fee.”"}, {"paragraph": 66, "text": "Sir James flushed slightly."}, {"paragraph": 67, "text": "“There is no question of a fee, Mr. Hersheimmer. I am not a private
detective.”"}, {"paragraph": 68, "text": "“Sorry. I guess I was just a mite hasty, but I’ve been feeling bad about
this money question. I wanted to offer a big reward for news of Jane
some days ago, but your crusted institution of Scotland Yard advised me
against it. Said it was undesirable.”"}, {"paragraph": 69, "text": "“They were probably right,” said Sir James dryly."}, {"paragraph": 70, "text": "“But it’s all O.K. about Julius,” put in Tuppence. “He’s not pulling
your leg. He’s got simply pots of money.”"}, {"paragraph": 71, "text": "“The old man piled it up in style,” explained Julius. “Now, let’s get
down to it. What’s your idea?”"}, {"paragraph": 72, "text": "Sir James considered for a moment or two."}, {"paragraph": 73, "text": "“There is no time to be lost. The sooner we strike the better.” He
turned to Tuppence. “Is Mrs. Vandemeyer dining out to-night, do you
know?”"}, {"paragraph": 74, "text": "“Yes, I think so, but she will not be out late. Otherwise, she would
have taken the latchkey.”"}, {"paragraph": 75, "text": "“Good. I will call upon her about ten o’clock. What time are you
supposed to return?”"}, {"paragraph": 76, "text": "“About nine-thirty or ten, but I could go back earlier.”"}, {"paragraph": 77, "text": "“You must not do that on any account. It might arouse suspicion if you
did not stay out till the usual time. Be back by nine-thirty. I will
arrive at ten. Mr. Hersheimmer will wait below in a taxi perhaps.”"}, {"paragraph": 78, "text": "“He’s got a new Rolls-Royce car,” said Tuppence with vicarious pride."}, {"paragraph": 79, "text": "“Even better. If I succeed in obtaining the address from her, we can
go there at once, taking Mrs. Vandemeyer with us if necessary. You
understand?”"}, {"paragraph": 80, "text": "“Yes.” Tuppence rose to her feet with a skip of delight. “Oh, I feel so
much better!”"}, {"paragraph": 81, "text": "“Don’t build on it too much, Miss Tuppence. Go easy.”"}, {"paragraph": 82, "text": "Julius turned to the lawyer."}, {"paragraph": 83, "text": "“Say, then. I’ll call for you in the car round about nine-thirty. Is
that right?”"}, {"paragraph": 84, "text": "“Perhaps that will be the best plan. It would be unnecessary to have two
cars waiting about. Now, Miss Tuppence, my advice to you is to go and
have a good dinner, a _really_ good one, mind. And don’t think ahead
more than you can help.”"}, {"paragraph": 85, "text": "He shook hands with them both, and a moment later they were outside."}, {"paragraph": 86, "text": "“Isn’t he a duck?” inquired Tuppence ecstatically, as she skipped down
the steps. “Oh, Julius, isn’t he just a duck?”"}, {"paragraph": 87, "text": "“Well, I allow he seems to be the goods all right. And I was wrong about
its being useless to go to him. Say, shall we go right away back to the
_Ritz?_”"}, {"paragraph": 88, "text": "“I must walk a bit, I think. I feel so excited. Drop me in the park,
will you? Unless you’d like to come too?”"}, {"paragraph": 89, "text": "“I want to get some petrol,” he explained. “And send off a cable or
two.”"}, {"paragraph": 90, "text": "“All right. I’ll meet you at the _Ritz_ at seven. We’ll have to dine
upstairs. I can’t show myself in these glad rags.”"}, {"paragraph": 91, "text": "“Sure. I’ll get Felix help me choose the menu. He’s some head waiter,
that. So long.”"}, {"paragraph": 92, "text": "Tuppence walked briskly along towards the Serpentine, first glancing at
her watch. It was nearly six o’clock. She remembered that she had had no
tea, but felt too excited to be conscious of hunger. She walked as
far as Kensington Gardens and then slowly retraced her steps, feeling
infinitely better for the fresh air and exercise. It was not so easy to
follow Sir James’s advice, and put the possible events of the evening
out of her head. As she drew nearer and nearer to Hyde Park corner, the
temptation to return to South Audley Mansions was almost irresistible."}, {"paragraph": 93, "text": "At any rate, she decided, it would do no harm just to go and _look_
at the building. Perhaps, then, she could resign herself to waiting
patiently for ten o’clock."}, {"paragraph": 94, "text": "South Audley Mansions looked exactly the same as usual. What Tuppence
had expected she hardly knew, but the sight of its red brick stolidity
slightly assuaged the growing and entirely unreasonable uneasiness
that possessed her. She was just turning away when she heard a piercing
whistle, and the faithful Albert came running from the building to join
her."}, {"paragraph": 95, "text": "Tuppence frowned. It was no part of the programme to have attention
called to her presence in the neighbourhood, but Albert was purple with
suppressed excitement."}, {"paragraph": 96, "text": "“I say, miss, she’s a-going!”"}, {"paragraph": 97, "text": "“Who’s going?” demanded Tuppence sharply."}, {"paragraph": 98, "text": "“The crook. Ready Rita. Mrs. Vandemeyer. She’s a-packing up, and she’s
just sent down word for me to get her a taxi.”"}, {"paragraph": 99, "text": "“What?” Tuppence clutched his arm."}, {"paragraph": 100, "text": "“It’s the truth, miss. I thought maybe as you didn’t know about it.”"}, {"paragraph": 101, "text": "“Albert,” cried Tuppence, “you’re a brick. If it hadn’t been for you
we’d have lost her.”"}, {"paragraph": 102, "text": "Albert flushed with pleasure at this tribute."}, {"paragraph": 103, "text": "“There’s no time to lose,” said Tuppence, crossing the road. “I’ve got
to stop her. At all costs I must keep her here until----” She broke off.
“Albert, there’s a telephone here, isn’t there?”"}, {"paragraph": 104, "text": "The boy shook his head."}, {"paragraph": 105, "text": "“The flats mostly have their own, miss. But there’s a box just round the
corner.”"}, {"paragraph": 106, "text": "“Go to it then, at once, and ring up the _Ritz Hotel_. Ask for Mr.
Hersheimmer, and when you get him tell him to get Sir James and come on
at once, as Mrs. Vandemeyer is trying to hook it. If you can’t get him,
ring up Sir James Peel Edgerton, you’ll find his number in the book, and
tell him what’s happening. You won’t forget the names, will you?”"}, {"paragraph": 107, "text": "Albert repeated them glibly. “You trust to me, miss, it’ll be all right.
But what about you? Aren’t you afraid to trust yourself with her?”"}, {"paragraph": 108, "text": "“No, no, that’s all right. _But go and telephone_. Be quick.”"}, {"paragraph": 109, "text": "Drawing a long breath, Tuppence entered the Mansions and ran up to the
door of No. 20. How she was to detain Mrs. Vandemeyer until the two men
arrived, she did not know, but somehow or other it had to be done, and
she must accomplish the task single-handed. What had occasioned this
precipitate departure? Did Mrs. Vandemeyer suspect her?"}, {"paragraph": 110, "text": "Speculations were idle. Tuppence pressed the bell firmly. She might
learn something from the cook."}, {"paragraph": 111, "text": "Nothing happened and, after waiting some minutes, Tuppence pressed the
bell again, keeping her finger on the button for some little while.
At last she heard footsteps inside, and a moment later Mrs. Vandemeyer
herself opened the door. She lifted her eyebrows at the sight of the
girl."}, {"paragraph": 112, "text": "“You?”"}, {"paragraph": 113, "text": "“I had a touch of toothache, ma’am,” said Tuppence glibly. “So thought
it better to come home and have a quiet evening.”"}, {"paragraph": 114, "text": "Mrs. Vandemeyer said nothing, but she drew back and let Tuppence pass
into the hall."}, {"paragraph": 115, "text": "“How unfortunate for you,” she said coldly. “You had better go to bed.”"}, {"paragraph": 116, "text": "“Oh, I shall be all right in the kitchen, ma’am. Cook will----”"}, {"paragraph": 117, "text": "“Cook is out,” said Mrs. Vandemeyer, in a rather disagreeable tone. “I
sent her out. So you see you had better go to bed.”"}, {"paragraph": 118, "text": "Suddenly Tuppence felt afraid. There was a ring in Mrs. Vandemeyer’s
voice that she did not like at all. Also, the other woman was slowly
edging her up the passage. Tuppence turned at bay."}, {"paragraph": 119, "text": "“I don’t want----”"}, {"paragraph": 120, "text": "Then, in a flash, a rim of cold steel touched her temple, and Mrs.
Vandemeyer’s voice rose cold and menacing:"}, {"paragraph": 121, "text": "“You damned little fool! Do you think I don’t know? No, don’t answer. If
you struggle or cry out, I’ll shoot you like a dog.”"}, {"paragraph": 122, "text": "The rim of steel pressed a little harder against the girl’s temple."}, {"paragraph": 123, "text": "“Now then, march,” went on Mrs. Vandemeyer. “This way--into my room. In
a minute, when I’ve done with you, you’ll go to bed as I told you to.
And you’ll sleep--oh yes, my little spy, you’ll sleep all right!”"}, {"paragraph": 124, "text": "There was a sort of hideous geniality in the last words which Tuppence
did not at all like. For the moment there was nothing to be done, and
she walked obediently into Mrs. Vandemeyer’s bedroom. The pistol never
left her forehead. The room was in a state of wild disorder, clothes
were flung about right and left, a suit-case and a hat box, half-packed,
stood in the middle of the floor."}, {"paragraph": 125, "text": "Tuppence pulled herself together with an effort. Her voice shook a
little, but she spoke out bravely."}, {"paragraph": 126, "text": "“Come now,” she said. “This is nonsense. You can’t shoot me. Why, every
one in the building would hear the report.”"}, {"paragraph": 127, "text": "“I’d risk that,” said Mrs. Vandemeyer cheerfully. “But, as long as you
don’t sing out for help, you’re all right--and I don’t think you will.
You’re a clever girl. You deceived _me_ all right. I hadn’t a suspicion
of you! So I’ve no doubt that you understand perfectly well that this
is where I’m on top and you’re underneath. Now then--sit on the bed. Put
your hands above your head, and if you value your life don’t move them.”"}, {"paragraph": 128, "text": "Tuppence obeyed passively. Her good sense told her that there was
nothing else to do but accept the situation. If she shrieked for help
there was very little chance of anyone hearing her, whereas there was
probably quite a good chance of Mrs. Vandemeyer’s shooting her. In the
meantime, every minute of delay gained was valuable."}, {"paragraph": 129, "text": "Mrs. Vandemeyer laid down the revolver on the edge of the washstand
within reach of her hand, and, still eyeing Tuppence like a lynx in case
the girl should attempt to move, she took a little stoppered bottle from
its place on the marble and poured some of its contents into a glass
which she filled up with water."}, {"paragraph": 130, "text": "“What’s that?” asked Tuppence sharply."}, {"paragraph": 131, "text": "“Something to make you sleep soundly.”"}, {"paragraph": 132, "text": "Tuppence paled a little."}, {"paragraph": 133, "text": "“Are you going to poison me?” she asked in a whisper."}, {"paragraph": 134, "text": "“Perhaps,” said Mrs. Vandemeyer, smiling agreeably."}, {"paragraph": 135, "text": "“Then I shan’t drink it,” said Tuppence firmly. “I’d much rather be
shot. At any rate that would make a row, and some one might hear it. But
I won’t be killed off quietly like a lamb.”"}, {"paragraph": 136, "text": "Mrs. Vandemeyer stamped her foot."}, {"paragraph": 137, "text": "“Don’t be a little fool! Do you really think I want a hue and cry for
murder out after me? If you’ve any sense at all, you’ll realize that
poisoning you wouldn’t suit my book at all. It’s a sleeping draught,
that’s all. You’ll wake up to-morrow morning none the worse. I simply
don’t want the bother of tying you up and gagging you. That’s the
alternative--and you won’t like it, I can tell you! I can be very rough
if I choose. So drink this down like a good girl, and you’ll be none the
worse for it.”"}, {"paragraph": 138, "text": "In her heart of hearts Tuppence believed her. The arguments she had
adduced rang true. It was a simple and effective method of getting her
out of the way for the time being. Nevertheless, the girl did not take
kindly to the idea of being tamely put to sleep without as much as one
bid for freedom. She felt that once Mrs. Vandemeyer gave them the slip,
the last hope of finding Tommy would be gone."}, {"paragraph": 139, "text": "Tuppence was quick in her mental processes. All these reflections
passed through her mind in a flash, and she saw where a chance, a very
problematical chance, lay, and she determined to risk all in one supreme
effort."}, {"paragraph": 140, "text": "Accordingly, she lurched suddenly off the bed and fell on her knees
before Mrs. Vandemeyer, clutching her skirts frantically."}, {"paragraph": 141, "text": "“I don’t believe it,” she moaned. “It’s poison--I know it’s poison.
Oh, don’t make me drink it”--her voice rose to a shriek--“don’t make me
drink it!”"}, {"paragraph": 142, "text": "Mrs. Vandemeyer, glass in hand, looked down with a curling lip at this
sudden collapse."}, {"paragraph": 143, "text": "“Get up, you little idiot! Don’t go on drivelling there. How you ever
had the nerve to play your part as you did I can’t think.” She stamped
her foot. “Get up, I say.”"}, {"paragraph": 144, "text": "But Tuppence continued to cling and sob, interjecting her sobs with
incoherent appeals for mercy. Every minute gained was to the good.
Moreover, as she grovelled, she moved imperceptibly nearer to her
objective."}, {"paragraph": 145, "text": "Mrs. Vandemeyer gave a sharp impatient exclamation, and jerked the girl
to her knees."}, {"paragraph": 146, "text": "“Drink it at once!” Imperiously she pressed the glass to the girl’s
lips."}, {"paragraph": 147, "text": "Tuppence gave one last despairing moan."}, {"paragraph": 148, "text": "“You swear it won’t hurt me?” she temporized."}, {"paragraph": 149, "text": "“Of course it won’t hurt you. Don’t be a fool.”"}, {"paragraph": 150, "text": "“Will you swear it?”"}, {"paragraph": 151, "text": "“Yes, yes,” said the other impatiently. “I swear it.”"}, {"paragraph": 152, "text": "Tuppence raised a trembling left hand to the glass."}, {"paragraph": 153, "text": "“Very well.” Her mouth opened meekly."}, {"paragraph": 154, "text": "Mrs. Vandemeyer gave a sigh of relief, off her guard for the moment.
Then, quick as a flash, Tuppence jerked the glass upward as hard as she
could. The fluid in it splashed into Mrs. Vandemeyer’s face, and during
her momentary gasp, Tuppence’s right hand shot out and grasped the
revolver where it lay on the edge of the washstand. The next moment
she had sprung back a pace, and the revolver pointed straight at Mrs.
Vandemeyer’s heart, with no unsteadiness in the hand that held it."}, {"paragraph": 155, "text": "In the moment of victory, Tuppence betrayed a somewhat unsportsmanlike

Her outstretched hand pointed over Tuppence’s head. Then she swayed to the ground in a dead faint."}, {"paragraph": 131, "text": "Tuppence looked round to see what had startled her."}, {"paragraph": 132, "text": "In the doorway were Sir James Peel Edgerton and Julius Hersheimmer."}], "015.source": [{"paragraph": 1, "text": "NOTHING was more surprising and bewildering to Tuppence than the ease
and simplicity with which everything was arranged, owing to Sir James’s

abroad, and that the servants had already left? Sir James and his young
friends had been paying a call upon her, when she was suddenly stricken
down and they had spent the night in the flat, not liking to leave
her alone. Did they know of any relatives? They did not, but Sir James
referred him to Mrs. Vandemeyer’s solicitor."}, {"paragraph": 2, "text": "Shortly afterwards a nurse arrived to take charge, and the other left
the ill-omened building."}, {"paragraph": 3, "text": "“And what now?” asked Julius, with a gesture of despair. “I guess we’re
down and out for good.”"}, {"paragraph": 4, "text": "Sir James stroked his chin thoughtfully."}, {"paragraph": 5, "text": "“No,” he said quietly. “There is still the chance that Dr. Hall may be
able to tell us something.”"}, {"paragraph": 6, "text": "“Gee! I’d forgotten him.”"}, {"paragraph": 7, "text": "“The chance is slight, but it must not be neglected. I think I told you
that he is staying at the _Métropole_. I should suggest that we call
upon him there as soon as possible. Shall we say after a bath and
breakfast?”"}, {"paragraph": 8, "text": "It was arranged that Tuppence and Julius should return to the _Ritz_,
and call for Sir James in the car. This programme was faithfully carried
out, and a little after eleven they drew up before the _Métropole_.
They asked for Dr. Hall, and a page-boy went in search of him. In a few
minutes the little doctor came hurrying towards them."}, {"paragraph": 9, "text": "“Can you spare us a few minutes, Dr. Hall?” said Sir James pleasantly.
“Let me introduce you to Miss Cowley. Mr. Hersheimmer, I think, you
already know.”"}, {"paragraph": 10, "text": "A quizzical gleam came into the doctor’s eye as he shook hands with
Julius."}, {"paragraph": 11, "text": "“Ah, yes, my young friend of the tree episode! Ankle all right, eh?”"}, {"paragraph": 12, "text": "“I guess it’s cured owing to your skilful treatment, doc.”"}, {"paragraph": 13, "text": "“And the heart trouble? Ha ha!”"}, {"paragraph": 14, "text": "“Still searching,” said Julius briefly."}, {"paragraph": 15, "text": "“To come to the point, can we have a word with you in private?” asked
Sir James."}, {"paragraph": 16, "text": "“Certainly. I think there is a room here where we shall be quite
undisturbed.”"}, {"paragraph": 17, "text": "He led the way, and the others followed him. They sat down, and the
doctor looked inquiringly at Sir James."}, {"paragraph": 18, "text": "“Dr. Hall, I am very anxious to find a certain young lady for the
purpose of obtaining a statement from her. I have reason to believe
that she has been at one time or another in your establishment at
Bournemouth. I hope I am transgressing no professional etiquette in
questioning you on the subject?”"}, {"paragraph": 19, "text": "“I suppose it is a matter of testimony?”"}, {"paragraph": 20, "text": "Sir James hesitated a moment, then he replied:"}, {"paragraph": 21, "text": "“Yes.”"}, {"paragraph": 22, "text": "“I shall be pleased to give you any information in my power. What is
the young lady’s name? Mr. Hersheimmer asked me, I remember----” He half
turned to Julius."}, {"paragraph": 23, "text": "“The name,” said Sir James bluntly, “is really immaterial. She would be
almost certainly sent to you under an assumed one. But I should like to
know if you are acquainted with a Mrs. Vandemeyer?”"}, {"paragraph": 24, "text": "“Mrs. Vandemeyer, of 20 South Audley Mansions? I know her slightly.”"}, {"paragraph": 25, "text": "“You are not aware of what has happened?”"}, {"paragraph": 26, "text": "“What do you mean?”"}, {"paragraph": 27, "text": "“You do not know that Mrs. Vandemeyer is dead?”"}, {"paragraph": 28, "text": "“Dear, dear, I had no idea of it! When did it happen?”"}, {"paragraph": 29, "text": "“She took an overdose of chloral last night.”"}, {"paragraph": 30, "text": "“Purposely?”"}, {"paragraph": 31, "text": "“Accidentally, it is believed. I should not like to say myself. Anyway,
she was found dead this morning.”"}, {"paragraph": 32, "text": "“Very sad. A singularly handsome woman. I presume she was a friend of
yours, since you are acquainted with all these details.”"}, {"paragraph": 33, "text": "“I am acquainted with the details because--well, it was I who found her
dead.”"}, {"paragraph": 34, "text": "“Indeed,” said the doctor, starting."}, {"paragraph": 35, "text": "“Yes,” said Sir James, and stroked his chin reflectively."}, {"paragraph": 36, "text": "“This is very sad news, but you will excuse me if I say that I do not
see how it bears on the subject of your inquiry?”"}, {"paragraph": 37, "text": "“It bears on it in this way, is it not a fact that Mrs. Vandemeyer
committed a young relative of hers to your charge?”"}, {"paragraph": 38, "text": "Julius leaned forward eagerly."}, {"paragraph": 39, "text": "“That is the case,” said the doctor quietly."}, {"paragraph": 40, "text": "“Under the name of----?”"}, {"paragraph": 41, "text": "“Janet Vandemeyer. I understood her to be a niece of Mrs. Vandemeyer’s.”"}, {"paragraph": 42, "text": "“And she came to you?”"}, {"paragraph": 43, "text": "“As far as I can remember in June or July of 1915.”"}, {"paragraph": 44, "text": "“Was she a mental case?”"}, {"paragraph": 45, "text": "“She is perfectly sane, if that is what you mean. I understood from Mrs.
Vandemeyer that the girl had been with her on the _Lusitania_ when
that ill-fated ship was sunk, and had suffered a severe shock in
consequence.”"}, {"paragraph": 46, "text": "“We’re on the right track, I think?” Sir James looked round."}, {"paragraph": 47, "text": "“As I said before, I’m a mutt!” returned Julius."}, {"paragraph": 48, "text": "The doctor looked at them all curiously."}, {"paragraph": 49, "text": "“You spoke of wanting a statement from her,” he said. “Supposing she is
not able to give one?”"}, {"paragraph": 50, "text": "“What? You have just said that she is perfectly sane.”"}, {"paragraph": 51, "text": "“So she is. Nevertheless, if you want a statement from her concerning
any events prior to May 7, 1915, she will not be able to give it to
you.”"}, {"paragraph": 52, "text": "They looked at the little man, stupefied. He nodded cheerfully."}, {"paragraph": 53, "text": "“It’s a pity,” he said. “A great pity, especially as I gather, Sir
James, that the matter is important. But there it is, she can tell you
nothing.”"}, {"paragraph": 54, "text": "“But why, man? Darn it all, why?”"}, {"paragraph": 55, "text": "The little man shifted his benevolent glance to the excited young
American."}, {"paragraph": 56, "text": "“Because Janet Vandemeyer is suffering from a complete loss of memory.”"}, {"paragraph": 57, "text": "_“What?”_"}, {"paragraph": 58, "text": "“Quite so. An interesting case, a _very_ interesting case. Not so
uncommon, really, as you would think. There are several very well known
parallels. It’s the first case of the kind that I’ve had under my own
personal observation, and I must admit that I’ve found it of absorbing
interest.” There was something rather ghoulish in the little man’s
satisfaction."}, {"paragraph": 59, "text": "“And she remembers nothing,” said Sir James slowly."}, {"paragraph": 60, "text": "“Nothing prior to May 7, 1915. After that date her memory is as good as
yours or mine.”"}, {"paragraph": 61, "text": "“Then the first thing she remembers?”"}, {"paragraph": 62, "text": "“Is landing with the survivors. Everything before that is a blank. She
did not know her own name, or where she had come from, or where she was.
She couldn’t even speak her own tongue.”"}, {"paragraph": 63, "text": "“But surely all this is most unusual?” put in Julius."}, {"paragraph": 64, "text": "“No, my dear sir. Quite normal under the circumstances. Severe shock to
the nervous system. Loss of memory proceeds nearly always on the same
lines. I suggested a specialist, of course. There’s a very good man in
Paris--makes a study of these cases--but Mrs. Vandemeyer opposed the
idea of publicity that might result from such a course.”"}, {"paragraph": 65, "text": "“I can imagine she would,” said Sir James grimly."}, {"paragraph": 66, "text": "“I fell in with her views. There is a certain notoriety given to these
cases. And the girl was very young--nineteen, I believe. It seemed
a pity that her infirmity should be talked about--might damage her
prospects. Besides, there is no special treatment to pursue in such
cases. It is really a matter of waiting.”"}, {"paragraph": 67, "text": "“Waiting?”"}, {"paragraph": 68, "text": "“Yes, sooner or later, the memory will return--as suddenly as it
went. But in all probability the girl will have entirely forgotten the
intervening period, and will take up life where she left off--at the
sinking of the _Lusitania_.”"}, {"paragraph": 69, "text": "“And when do you expect this to happen?”"}, {"paragraph": 70, "text": "The doctor shrugged his shoulders."}, {"paragraph": 71, "text": "“Ah, that I cannot say. Sometimes it is a matter of months, sometimes
it has been known to be as long as twenty years! Sometimes another shock
does the trick. One restores what the other took away.”"}, {"paragraph": 72, "text": "“Another shock, eh?” said Julius thoughtfully."}, {"paragraph": 73, "text": "“Exactly. There was a case in Colorado----” The little man’s voice
trailed on, voluble, mildly enthusiastic."}, {"paragraph": 74, "text": "Julius did not seem to be listening. He had relapsed into his own
thoughts and was frowning. Suddenly he came out of his brown study,
and hit the table such a resounding bang with his fist that every one
jumped, the doctor most of all."}, {"paragraph": 75, "text": "“I’ve got it! I guess, doc, I’d like your medical opinion on the plan
I’m about to outline. Say Jane was to cross the herring pond again, and
the same thing was to happen. The submarine, the sinking ship, every one
to take to the boats--and so on. Wouldn’t that do the trick? Wouldn’t it
give a mighty big bump to her subconscious self, or whatever the jargon
is, and start it functioning again right away?”"}, {"paragraph": 76, "text": "“A very interesting speculation, Mr. Hersheimmer. In my own opinion, it
would be successful. It is unfortunate that there is no chance of the
conditions repeating themselves as you suggest.”"}, {"paragraph": 77, "text": "“Not by nature, perhaps, doc. But I’m talking about art.”"}, {"paragraph": 78, "text": "“Art?”"}, {"paragraph": 79, "text": "“Why, yes. What’s the difficulty? Hire a liner----”"}, {"paragraph": 80, "text": "“A liner!” murmured Dr. Hall faintly."}, {"paragraph": 81, "text": "“Hire some passengers, hire a submarine--that’s the only difficulty, I
guess. Governments are apt to be a bit hide-bound over their engines of
war. They won’t sell to the first-comer. Still, I guess that can be got
over. Ever heard of the word ‘graft,’ sir? Well, graft gets there every
time! I reckon that we shan’t really need to fire a torpedo. If every
one hustles round and screams loud enough that the ship is sinking, it
ought to be enough for an innocent young girl like Jane. By the time
she’s got a life-belt on her, and is being hustled into a boat, with
a well-drilled lot of artistes doing the hysterical stunt on deck,
why--she ought to be right back where she was in May, 1915. How’s that
for the bare outline?”"}, {"paragraph": 82, "text": "Dr. Hall looked at Julius. Everything that he was for the moment
incapable of saying was eloquent in that look."}, {"paragraph": 83, "text": "“No,” said Julius, in answer to it, “I’m not crazy. The thing’s
perfectly possible. It’s done every day in the States for the movies.
Haven’t you seen trains in collision on the screen? What’s the
difference between buying up a train and buying up a liner? Get the
properties and you can go right ahead!”"}, {"paragraph": 84, "text": "Dr. Hall found his voice."}, {"paragraph": 85, "text": "“But the expense, my dear sir.” His voice rose. “The expense! It will be
_colossal!_”"}, {"paragraph": 86, "text": "“Money doesn’t worry me any,” explained Julius simply."}, {"paragraph": 87, "text": "Dr. Hall turned an appealing face to Sir James, who smiled slightly."}, {"paragraph": 88, "text": "“Mr. Hersheimmer is very well off--very well off indeed.”"}, {"paragraph": 89, "text": "The doctor’s glance came back to Julius with a new and subtle quality in
it. This was no longer an eccentric young fellow with a habit of falling
off trees. The doctor’s eyes held the deference accorded to a really
rich man."}, {"paragraph": 90, "text": "“Very remarkable plan. Very remarkable,” he murmured. “The movies--of
course! Your American word for the kinema. Very interesting. I fear we
are perhaps a little behind the times over here in our methods. And you
really mean to carry out this remarkable plan of yours.”"}, {"paragraph": 91, "text": "“You bet your bottom dollar I do.”"}, {"paragraph": 92, "text": "The doctor believed him--which was a tribute to his nationality. If an

to his sanity."}, {"paragraph": 93, "text": "“I cannot guarantee a cure,” he pointed out. “Perhaps I ought to make
that quite clear.”"}, {"paragraph": 94, "text": "“Sure, that’s all right,” said Julius. “You just trot out Jane, and
leave the rest to me.”"}, {"paragraph": 95, "text": "“Jane?”"}, {"paragraph": 96, "text": "“Miss Janet Vandemeyer, then. Can we get on the long distance to your
